history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration define the specific areas of cybersecurity that need to be accountable to a central governance function and encourage all entities to participate in global cybersecurity initiatives to increase visibility of and strengthen ICT security.
history.administration_response: The following specific areas have been identified as needing to be accountable to a central governance function, tools and mechanisms to monitor performance have been, or are in the process of being, deployed as part of global initiatives: (a) information security awareness training, and proactive simulation exercises; (b) response to security advisories that require, for example, deployment for security updates; (c) compliance with access control procedures; (d) network segmentation; (e) security incident reporting and response; (f) proactive vulnerability management; and (g) comprehensive deployment and operation of the threat- hunting solution.
history.board_assessment: Given that there is no significant improvement about the ICT security, the Board considers the recommendation to be under implementation.

III. Status of implementation of recommendations on the Umoja system In annex II to its report on the United Nations for the year ended 31 December 2023, the Board provided a summary of the status of implementation of its 17 extant recommendations on the Umoja system relating to prior financial periods. Of the 17 extant recommendations, 8 (47 per cent) had been implemented, 3 (18 per cent) had been overtaken by events and the other 6 (35 per cent) were under implementation. Table 5 presents a summary of the overall situation, as of August 2024 with respect to the six recommendations that were determined by the Board to be under implementation as of December 2023. Of those outstanding recommendations, closure has been requested for one while three are scheduled to be implemented in 2024, one in 2025 and one in 2026. history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration define the specific areas of cybersecurity that need to be accountable to a central governance function, and encourage all entities to participate in global cybersecurity initiatives to increase visibility of and strengthen cybersecurity.
history.administration_response: This recommendation overlaps with the recommendation contained in paragraph 531 of A/79/5 (Vol. I). In that recommendation, the Board requested the Administration to clearly define the scope of ICT security, including key central and local roles and responsibilities, in the accountability framework. The Office of Information and Communications Technology is in the process of incorporating the definition of the scope of ICT security, including specific central and local roles and responsibilities, into the ICT accountability framework. When the recommendation contained in paragraph 531 of A/79/5 (Vol. I) is implemented, the recommendation contained in paragraph 601 of A/78/5 (Vol. I) is expected to be closed. Given this overlap, the Office requests that the recommendation contained in paragraph 601 of A/78/5 (Vol. I) be closed and that the recommendation contained in paragraph 531 of A/79/5 (Vol. I) be maintained.
history.board_assessment: Given that the accountability framework contains information on cybersecurity roles and responsibilities, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
